title: Paper Simplicial Discovery
subtitle: Higher-Order Scientific Literature Exploration and Hypothesis Generation with Simplicial Complexes and LLMs
byline: Paper Simplicial Discovery Team · OSI Hackathon 2026
abstract: Scientific advances often arise from combining ideas that sit in different research communities. Conventional literature retrieval commonly focuses on isolated papers or pairwise semantic similarity, leaving larger combinations difficult to explore systematically. We present Paper Simplicial Discovery, a working prototype that represents scientific papers as a similarity graph, lifts mutually linked paper triplets into a simplicial complex, ranks these triads, and uses an LLM to critically assess their potential for hypothesis generation. From 45,666 papers in the CoreX subset, the pipeline retains 42,164 distinct papers, constructs 94,180 triangles, and ranks 1,000 candidates. Detailed assessment of 25 triads produces 125 candidate research hypotheses. An interactive explorer exposes the literature evidence and generated suggestions. The method supports human-led, interdisciplinary scientific ideation; the hypotheses are not yet experimentally validated.

sections.heading: Motivation and contribution
paragraphs: Scientific literature is growing faster than any individual researcher can read. Search and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) help locate related documents, but relatedness alone is not a research hypothesis. In particular, pairwise links A ∼ B and B ∼ C do not establish a compelling joint connection among all three papers.

Our contribution is a higher-order discovery layer between retrieval and language-model reasoning. Rather than asking an LLM to propose scientific ideas from an unstructured collection, we identify mutually connected triples of research papers, extract scientific evidence from each triple, and request critical assessment and testable hypotheses grounded in all three sources. This separates scalable candidate generation from deeper scientific synthesis.
sections.pullquote: Pairwise similarity finds neighbors; filled 2-simplices flag mutual three-way alignment worth human review.

subsections.title: Corpus representation
subsections.body: We use a 45,666-paper subset of the multidisciplinary CoreX corpus. Papers are embedded using mean-pooled MatSciBERT representations. Near-duplicate items are merged using a cosine-similarity threshold of 0.99, retaining N = 42,164 papers.

subsections.title: Graph construction
subsections.body: A k-nearest-neighbor graph with k = 5 connects semantically related papers; union symmetrization produces an undirected graph G = (V, E) with |E| = 166,993. Edges carry cosine similarities s_ij of the learned document embeddings.

subsections.title: Simplicial lifting
subsections.body: Using TopoNetX, we construct the clique-based rank-2 skeleton. A triplet T = {i, j, k} forms a 2-simplex when all three edges (i, j), (j, k), and (i, k) occur in G. This produces 94,180 triangles. The topological representation encodes mutual three-paper relatedness, although a triangle by itself does not guarantee scientific synergy.

subsections.title: Candidate ranking
subsections.body: We rank triangles using the geometric mean of edge similarities, penalized by the weakest edge: S(T) = (s_ij s_jk s_ik)^(1/3) · min{s_ij, s_jk, s_ik}. Language and academic-science filters limit low-quality candidates. We preserve the 1,000 highest-ranked triads for interactive review and select the top 25 for deeper LLM assessment.

subsections.title: Evidence and hypothesis synthesis
subsections.body: For each selected paper, a structured digest extracts aims and problem formulation, motivation, methodology, and findings. A Gemini-based evaluator receives three digests and pairwise similarity scores. It distinguishes genuine complementarity from superficial shared vocabulary, assigns a quality rating, and proposes five candidate hypotheses integrating all three papers—with mechanisms, applications, and feasibility judgments. All judgments are model-generated and require expert verification.

sections.heading: Prototype and results
paragraphs: Our Python pipeline implements GPU-assisted graph construction, TopoNetX lifting, triad scoring, digest extraction, and structured LLM assessments. A lightweight web application lets users search 1,000 triads, inspect paper metadata, read evaluations, and navigate 125 candidate hypotheses—making the prototype inspectable rather than presenting ideas as untraceable chatbot answers.

Each selected triplet is rated on a 1–10 quality scale with thematic coherence, methodological complementarity, and non-triviality. The evaluator classifies triplets as genuine synergy, moderate overlap, or spurious co-occurrence. Five hypotheses per triplet include a mechanistic bridge and feasibility judgment.

Among 25 LLM-reviewed triads: 11 genuine cross-disciplinary synergy, 9 moderate overlap, 5 spurious. Quality scores range from 2.2 to 8.7 (mean 6.50/10). The five spurious cases highlight a failure mode: high embedding similarity may reflect writing conventions or generic terms—not substantive complementarity. Triangle enumeration is candidate generation; LLM critique is exploratory screening, not proof of novelty.

sections.heading: Illustrative scientific directions

examples.title: Energy-system decarbonization
examples.body: A high-ranked triad combines building-energy optimization, catalytic ethanol steam reforming, and offshore-wind HVDC transmission. The LLM suggested coupled modeling linking wind dispatch, chemical energy conversion, and dynamic urban demand—a concrete multi-physics integration avenue pending techno-economic validation.

examples.title: Microfluidics and mechanophenotyping
examples.body: Another triad joins electrically manipulated droplets, optical-tweezer cell mechanics, and magnetic nanostructures—proposing combined magnetic and dielectrophoretic microfluidics for mechanical screening, spanning soft matter, microfluidics, and biomedical instrumentation.

examples.title: Chemistry and responsive nanomaterials
examples.body: A third triad (LLM score 8.7/10) links optical-tweezer mechanics, responsive polymer nanogels, and peptide probes for curved lipid membranes—suggesting nanogel exosome mimics to calibrate mechanical measurements and probe curvature recognition.

sections.footnote: These examples trace to specific input publications. They illustrate hypothesis formulation, not confirmed discoveries.

sections.heading: Limitations and next steps
paragraphs: The system prioritizes local similarity, which can favor shared writing conventions over complementary but distant ideas. Clique triangles represent mutual proximity, not proven mechanistic interactions. A single model’s judgments cannot establish novelty, feasibility, or correctness; controlled comparison against standard RAG, pairwise retrieval, or expert questions is not yet complete.

Planned validation includes blinded expert scoring of plausibility, complementarity, originality, and experimental specificity—and reporting agreement between humans and the LLM. Future work adds citation- and method-aware novelty checks, diversity-aware triad selection, and larger simplicial structures with pruning. The broader goal is an evidence-linked ideation assistant that helps researchers notice overlooked connections while retaining human judgment.
